ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there are coordinate axes, and an ascending straight line passing through the origin O represents y1=x; there is also a parabola opening upward, which intersects the straight line at the origin O and at the upper-right point A, and the question stem gives the coordinates of A as (4,4). Reasoning: Point A(4,4) lies on the quadratic function y2=x^2-bx, so 4=4^2-4b=16-4b, solving gives b=3. Thus y2=x^2-3x. It is required that y1<y2, that is, x<x^2-3x; moving terms gives x^2-4x>0, that is, x(x-4)>0. When the product is greater than 0, the two factors have the same sign, therefore x<0 or x>4.

method.method_draft: Algebraic route: First note from the image that the straight line and the upward-opening parabola intersect at the origin O and at point A on the line. From the text, use A(4,4) as a point on y2=x^2-bx: 4=16-4b, so b=3. Then compare the two functions by solving y1<y2: x<x^2-3x, hence x^2-4x>0, or x(x-4)>0. By the sign rule for a product with roots 0 and 4, the solution is x<0 or x>4.
